answer: Make each agent identity pay for trust in verifiable work, not claims: before it can transact, a new identity must complete a history of useful attestations that cost real compute and time. Spinning up ten thousand clones then costs ten thousand times the work, which prices out mass sybils while honest agents pass once. Like pigment that stains only the surface it touches, reputation must stick to one identity and never transfer; a raven copying another agent's credentials still arrives empty-handed at the inlet, because the ledger checks the work history behind the name, not the name itself.
